answers.reason: The Nahor candidate explicitly identifies its location as Nahuru, matching the settlement near Haran associated with GEN 24:10.
Nuhashe (Nuhashshe) is a region of northern Syria. None of the candidates denotes that region; Ir-nahash is a settlement associated with Judah.
The Pethor candidate explicitly gives Pitru as another name, matching the Mesopotamian settlement associated with Balaam in NUM 22:5 and DEU 23:4.
Punt is the ancient trading region associated with the southern Red Sea. The Put candidate explicitly denotes Libya, and the other candidates are unrelated places.
Ragmat is identified here with Najran in southern Arabia. None of the Hamath or Ramah candidates has that location.
Salona is the ancient city in Dalmatia near modern Split. It is distinct from the Cretan promontory Salmone and all the other candidate settlements.
Saparda is placed in Asia Minor, whereas the candidates denote places in the Levant. No candidate identifies this settlement.
Saparre is located near Nippur in Babylonia. Sahar, Jerusalem's Parbar, and the Pharpar River near Damascus are different referents.
Scythia denotes the region associated with the Scythians around and beyond the northern Black Sea. None of the candidates denotes that region.
Sparta is the Greek city in Laconia associated with the Spartans in 1 Maccabees. Sarepta, Patara, and the other candidates are different places.
